LESSON: DANCE PRODUCTION

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10
Subject: MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT
Strand: Foundations of Music and Dance
Topic 1.7: Dance Production
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 12

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Dance Production, part of Foundations of Music and Dance in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade 10 MUSIC AND DANCE FOR LEARNERS WITH PHYSICAL IMPAIRMENT.

Key inquiry question: How can costumes and props be used to communicate the theme in a dance performance?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. in pairs or purposive groups, watch a variety of dances and discuss the elements of dance. Learners with postural defects 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. in pairs or purposive groups, watch a variety of dances and discuss the elements of dance. Learners with postural defects 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Dance Production together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Digital Literacy: The learner uses digital devices to record and listen to music performances.

• Collaboration: The learner works with others in groups as they source and design costumes for dance.

• Self-efficacy: The learner applies multimedia effects in production of a dance performance during a school event.

Values:
• Patriotism: The learner takes pride in using Kenyan signature outfits such as Maasai outfits for dance production

• Respect: The learner accommodates others’ ideas in group activities as they use digital audio applications.

• Integrity: The learner exercises honesty while recording their own sounds.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

• Road safety: the learner chooses a dance theme based on a risk awareness and management on road use and design an

appropriate costume.

• Peer Education and Mentorship: The learner assists others in groups as they record music.

• Social Cohesion: The learner actively participates in group choreography of cultural dance.

• Resource Mobilization and Utilization: The learner makes proper use of popular music from the community.

Suggested Learning Resources

ICT devices, Internet connectivity, Traditional Instruments, Portfolios, Anecdotal records Props and costumes, Resource

persons, Audio/visual recordings African dances and Textbooks
